newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends mixed, bull spreading props Dec.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends mixed, bull spreading props Dec.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed mixed with nearby December coming alive in late dealings on bull spreading and commercial buying amid renewed talk about a tight supply of high quality soft red winter wheat in the United States, traders said.
"We still need to attract good quality soft wheat to the eastern belt and that's why the spread is acting the way it is," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
The December/March spread narrowed Friday to roughly 12-1/2 cents per bushel premium Dec, a 3-1/4 cent change from Thursday's close.

Cargill Inc bought two million bushels of December, LIT America and Refco Inc each were late purchasers of the December and LFG Futures was the chief spreader, roughly of one million bushels, of the December/March, the traders said.
A drop in corn and soybean futures amid nearly ideal harvest activity pressed prices as did follow through technical selling, they said.
Technicians said the sharply lower close in wheat Thursday contributed to the bearish technical picture.
Wheat closed one cent higher to five cents lower, with December up one at $4.21.
Increased supplies of wheat worldwide also weighed on the market with the market weighing the pros and cons of a recent cut in USDA's estimate for U.S. wheat stocks as of September 1.

December wheat reached a session low of $4.13-1/2 per bushel and the nine-day relative strength index (RSI) at 35.031 was about the same as Thursday's closing level of 35. The market generally considers an RSI of 20 or less as an oversold market. The first support level for December was at $4.16-1/4 and the second support level was $4.08-1/4.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 17,000 contracts, down slightly from 17,534 Thursday.

In wheat options, Refco Inc bought 700 December $4.50 calls at three to 3-1/4 cents, and Cargill Investor Services bought 400 March $3.70 puts and sold 400 March $4.30 puts at five cents, the traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 8,000 contracts, down from 8,720 Thursday.
